{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABcngJ3A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGJzDw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 127, "title": "Support large PC-9821 IDE HDI images beyond 32 MiB with memory-efficient browser I/O", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator's PC-9821Ap DOS IDE HDD accepts **HDI files only up to 32 MiB**, which is far too small for installing and retaining multiple historical PC-98 DOS games. The user explicitly requests a substantially larger capacity, not a cosmetic change.

The 32 MiB limit is **a project-imposed implementation guard, not a physical PC-9821Ap storage limit**:

- [`src/hdd.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/hdd.rs): `MAX_HDI_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024`, checked by `HardDisk::parse`; HDI header size/offset and 512-byte CHS/IDE geometry are validated.
- [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs): Wasm `input_buffer` rejects images above that cap, the insert path clones the transfer buffer into a separate `Vec<u8>`, and export clones the whole disk again.
- [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js): the 32 MiB upload guard; `File.arrayBuffer()`, transfer into linear Wasm memory, and whole-HD I export. Large images therefore produce large transient memory copies and potentially a sluggish or OOM browser.
- [`src/firmware.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/firmware.rs): PC-98 synthetic IDE/SASI BIOS and [`src/hdd.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/hdd.rs) support bounded CHS/LBA access and report geometry/capacity, but must be validated beyond the formerly tested small disks.

**Do not merely raise `MAX_HDI_BYTES` to a huge number.** That would remove one rejection path while risking multi-gigabyte memory duplication, long transfers and misleading claims that all guest DOS configurations support the capacity.

## Expected outcome

Make the Ap profile useful for real DOS-game installs on **hundreds-of-megabytes HDI images**, with **512 MiB as the mandatory practical capacity target** and **1 GiB as a desired tested capacity where supported by the chosen HDI geometry, browser and guest**. Avoid arbitrary 32 MiB rejection; accept otherwise valid large HDI up to a justified format/resource boundary with clear errors when the actual environment cannot support an operation.

Implement a **coherent, bounded large-disk design** for local image import, emulated 512-byte IDE PIO and BIOS reads/writes, guest partition/filesystem access, reset, disk replacement and export, without constructing gratuitous complete copies of each disk in JavaScript *and* Wasm. Prefer an independently designed sparse/page-based or externally backed disk abstraction when needed; preserve synchronous guest-visible IDE semantics and deterministic execution. No emulator-library or other-emulator-code reuse.

**Do not conflate this with a different requested convenience feature**: automatically provisioning a formatted HDD when the browser opens. A default guest-installation disk/create-HDD button can be tracked separately; this Issue is about the scalable support for large user-selected HDIs, which is a prerequisite for that workflow.

## Technical scope

1. **Establish format bounds:** inspect the existing HDI header's 32-bit offset/size/cylinder/head/sector fields, arithmetic overflow checks, physical 512-byte sector mapping, CHS and 28-bit LBA selection, `IDENTIFY DEVICE` capacity words 60/61, BIOS INT 1Bh/INT 11h behavior and 32-bit/16-bit guest addressing. Distinguish HDI container limits, emulated IDE limits, guest DOS partition/FAT limits and practical browser memory limits. Do not invent geometry or silently truncate a large volume.
2. **Bound allocations and copies:** trace byte counts throughout browser `File` handling, Wasm buffer allocation, Rust `Machine::insert`, reads/writes, export and test inspection. Avoid multiple simultaneous whole-image copies or unbounded array expansion. Design a data plane appropriate for large local disks (file-backed/chunk-based reads or economical in-memory backing with bounded copies and dirty-sector overlays as justified). Keep private media local; no server upload.
3. **Correct guest-visible large capacity:** exercise CHS and LBA accesses to low, middle, high and last sectors; multi-sector reads/writes crossing boundaries; IDENTIFY, BIOS parameter reporting, IRQ/error/residual behavior; write protection of invalid out-of-capacity accesses; reset/mount/eject and persistence. All offsets/indexes must be overflow-safe and match actual header/capacity.
4. **Preserve complete round-trip:** after game/DOS writes, `Export disk` reconstructs an HDI with its original header, partition table and unchanged sectors intact and modified sectors correct. Test reimport and actual guest-visible persistence. Avoid JSONifying entire byte arrays, page-count-driven premature timeouts, and downloads that allocate another giant intermediate object if a more efficient path exists. Fail clearly and safely if a browser's resource limits preclude export; never corrupt or silently truncate.
5. **Real DOS usability:** run an independently prepared, rights-cleared PC-98 IDE HDI with a legitimate FAT12/FAT16 filesystem and test DOS read/write and a responsive shell, ideally across a volume or partition beyond the old 32 MiB bound; report separately if the actual guest DOS variant itself has a partition/volume-size limitation. No change of OS or guest-specific hack to claim capacity.
6. **Scope and preservation:** keep PC-9801VM's no-IDE rule, preserve floppy Auto routing, boot source selection, boot-with-floppy and HDD attached, IRQ/mouse/media interfaces, guest disk write semantics and existing small HDIs. Do not ship gigabyte fixtures, private game media, external BIOS, ROM/font dumps, or source code from existing emulators.

## Reproduction

1. Use [the browser demo](https://takahirox.github.io/pc98-rust/), default PC-9821Ap DOS + Auto, and select a correctly formed `.hdi` exceeding 32 MiB. Currently it is rejected with `HDI exceeds 32 MiB.`.
2. Verify the same container against `HardDisk::parse`; it is rejected by the fixed 32 MiB check before the valid geometry can be used.
3. A larger-file-supported implementation should accept a valid image and perform real IDE/BIOS access, read/write/reset/export, not merely display its filename or pass a parser-only unit test.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document specific **HDI format vs device vs guest vs browser** limits and why the old 32 MiB cap existed in this implementation. Remove the arbitrary 32 MiB restriction consistently in Rust, Wasm and browser UI, replacing it only with explicit, justified and correctly reported format/resource constraints. At minimum, **512 MiB valid HDI images are accepted and usable in the Ap browser and native core**; validate **1 GiB** where the designed representation and supported geometry permit, without claiming untested sizes.
- [ ] Independently test valid and malformed HDI headers, geometry/capacity multiplication, non-512 sectors, overflowed offsets, truncated/oversized files and unsupported device addressing. Reject invalid inputs without host panic, unbounded allocation or guest memory corruption. Never allocate based solely on an untrusted header before validating the input extent.
- [ ] Add native **large-disk boundary** tests for IDE IDENTIFY and BIOS geometry, CHS/LBA first/middle/last/out-of-range addresses, reads, writes, IRQ/error behavior, multi-sector transfers and reset. Select economical **sparse/chunked** fixtures/temporary files that do not commit large test media or make CI pay for many redundant full-disk traversals.
- [ ] Add full production release-Wasm Chromium acceptance of a representative **at least 512 MiB HDI** on the real Ap IDE path, covering upload/attach, guest-owned read/write (including beyond 32 MiB), reset, correct export/reimport and preserved untouched bytes, both at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Tests must assert real guest results, not script simulated disk success; avoid massive buffers in Playwright RPC and giant downloadable fixture artifacts.
- [ ] Measure and document browser input/export peak memory and time behavior for large media. Ensure the design doesn't create unnecessary simultaneous complete images in JS/Wasm, or stall a browser for pathological synchronous transfers. Provide helpful, recoverable errors when genuine browser memory/file constraints are reached, without losing previously mounted disk data.
- [ ] Verify the existing legal FreeDOS(98) HDD shell (and preferably a rights-cleared FAT16 disk whose partition extends past 32 MiB) still boots, reads/writes and executes actual guest DOS commands. A large parser alone is insufficient for guest **installation** support; record any independent DOS partition/installer limits instead of claiming universal support.
- [ ] Preserve existing 4–32 MiB HDIs, FDD1/FDD2/Auto routing, profile switches, reset, eject/export, the approved-public-assets audit and all existing storage tests. Document revised user-facing size guidance without implying that the browser bundles a large preformatted disk.
- [ ] Run applicable fixture/source/license preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Wasm build, and the complete real-Wasm Chromium suite at both serving roots. Apply the project's [performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles): verify the expensive large-image scenario without multiplying huge tests across irrelevant combinations, and record actual runtimes/peak memory and all failures.
- [ ] Use English Issue/PR/review/commit communications and independent original Rust/JS implementation. No proprietary OS/game media or user-specific HDI in Git, CI, artifacts or Pages; no required human/manual or post-merge checks before merge.

## Optional validation

For legally held local-only media, test larger PC-98 DOS game-installation images or installer workflows without sharing their bytes or adult game content. A separate feature can add a default preformatted installable HDD or Create HDD control and browser persistence once the capacity/data-plane foundations are robust.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Published Pages checks or genuine deployment-only issues must not be pre-merge blockers; use a separate `task` for operational failures.
